<reason>A (CON) won a close, high-quality debate by controlling the motion's operative meaning. A's opening judo — every example PRO trusts resolves physically (Maya Bay caps, Hallstatt bus limits, superbloom closure, Gion property rules) or voluntarily (Jackson Hole) — held up through five rounds; B never produced a case where the motion's distinctive tool (limits on third-party geotagging/promotion) demonstrably protected a site. A's dilemma (narrow reading prevents none of the cited harms; broad reading is vague and discriminatory) was never cleanly answered — B's "the motion does not specify the instrument" was exposed as unfalsifiable, and B's closing merely reasserted the narrow reading without addressing its emptiness. B landed real blows: the aggregation mechanism (conceded real by A), the upstream/prediction hinge, and the "gates plus limits vs gates alone" comparative. But A answered each: prediction is symmetric, physical responses deploy in days, takedowns chase fame already spread through news and hashtags — and B's own anchor case, the superbloom, was pin-independent. A's closing crisply crystallized "recruitment is not arrival" and pre-defused B's concession-play. Both sides showed strong grounding discipline, proper Q/A formatting, and only minor tail-end clipping.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's Pressure Q1 (name one cited harm the narrowed motion would have prevented, given the superbloom spread via unmonetized posts and news) paired with Rebuttal 2's A1 dilemma. B answered with Jackson Hole — a success story, not a prevented harm, and a voluntary campaign at that — leaving A's charge standing that the motion either binds third parties and fails, or binds only destinations' own feeds and prevents nothing.</best_rebuttal>
